items.summary: This paper presents the design and preliminary evaluation of KR A1, a humanoid-robot interaction prototype that integrates personalized voice synthesis, contextual dialogue processing, and emotion-aware response generation for potential mental-healthcare applications.

items.title: Improving Large Audio-Language Model Embedding Baselines for Instruction-Aware Speech Retrieval
items.summary: Speech retrieval finds relevant spoken documents given a spoken query. Instruction-aware speech retrieval expresses this goal through a natural-language text instruction. Large audio-language models (LALMs) effectively process speech and text, and our analysis shows that different retrieval requirements favor hidden states from different audio-encoder layers.

items.title: Full-sphere emission and reception directivities of seven echolocating bat species
items.summary: Echolocating bats shape their calls and the returning echoes with their noseleaf or mouth, head and pinnae. We describe a dataset of simulated far-field emission and reception directivities of seven echolocating bat species from three families (Phyllostomidae, Rhinolophidae and Vespertilionidae).

items.title: REAL: Reward Modeling through Evidence-Linked Analysis of Lifelikeness in Generated Speech
items.summary: Because large-scale listening tests are costly and slow, speech reward models can serve as scalable automatic judges for comparing generated utterances, curating data, and supporting iterative TTS development. We introduce REAL, a framework for Reward modeling through Evidence-linked Analysis of Lifelikeness in generated speech.

items.title: Nemotron 3 Diarization: Advancing the Accuracy-Efficiency Frontier in Streaming Speaker Diarization
items.summary: Streaming Sortformer introduced an arrival-order speaker cache to maintain speaker identities across chunks in end-to-end streaming speaker diarization, with a single model supporting configurable latency profiles spanning offline operation to ultra-low-latency streaming.

items.title: SCLAP: Temporal structural alignment improves localization in long-form audio
items.summary: This discards temporal structure and impairs both retrieval and localization, especially for short events in long recordings. On short-form audio (i.e., Clotho and TACOS datasets with 15-30s recordings), SCLAP remains competitive for retrieval while improving zero-shot localization over CLAP and Text-aware Attention Pooling.

items.title: Discriminator-free adversarial domain adaptation for robust speech classification
items.summary: The performance of speech classification systems such as speech emotion recognition or pathological speech detection can degrade substantially when there is a domain shift between training and test data. In this paper, we propose to use a discriminator-free adversarial learning network (DALN) for unsupervised domain adaptation in speech classification tasks.

items.title: CallCleaner: Lightweight Bioacoustic Denoising from an Audio Foundation Model
items.summary: Many studies of animal vocalizations require clean recordings, but animals are usually recorded in the field, with background noise from weather, vehicles, and other animals. We show that a general-purpose source separation foundation model, SAM-Audio, removes more noise than either of these types of methods, when used without training and prompted with time spans from a simple animal VAD.

items.title: Capability-Guided Iterative Online Optimization of Cascaded Spoken-Dialogue Modules
items.summary: We study iterative optimization of the first and last modules. After only 200 steps for Whisper and 600 for CosyVoice2 of our iterative online optimization, we observe that, on the Chinese MAGICDATA-RAMC dataset, Whisper reduces CER from 14.18% to 10.77%, while CosyVoice2 reduces it from 4.78% to 4.04%.

items.title: Task-adaptive anonymisation enables privacy-preserving sharing of clinical speech data
items.summary: Clinical speech is increasingly used for disease screening and clinical assessment, but directly distributing speech recordings poses privacy risks because they contain both speaker-identifying voiceprints and sensitive spoken content.

items.title: Virtual-Flow: Virtual Microphone-based Speech Enhancement via Semi-supervised Flow Matching
items.summary: Neural network-based virtual microphone estimation (neural-VME) synthesizes microphone signals at unobserved spatial locations from a limited set of real microphone (RM) physical recordings.

items.title: Pandemonium: Longform Target-Speaker Speech Recognition with Cross-Speaker Interactions
items.summary: Diarization-conditioned target-speaker ASR (TS-ASR), in particular Diarization-conditioned Whisper (DiCoW), is an accurate and data-efficient approach to multi-talker transcription. It has, however, three structural limitations: the model transcribes each speaker independently, operates on short (30 s) windows, and optimizes its diarization and TS-ASR components separately.

items.title: BAmbiDrop: Array-Agnostic Speech Enhancement with Zero-Shot binaural Reproduction using Multi-center Ambisonics Encoding
items.summary: Array-agnostic enhancement networks generalize across microphone geometries but produce a single channel, while binaural enhancement methods preserve interaural cues only for one fixed device geometry. We propose BAmbiDrop, a framework that extends array-agnostic enhancement to binaural reproduction without retraining.

items.title: Lightweight Neural Prediction for MDCT-Based Perceptual Audio Coding
items.summary: Perceptual audio codecs often use predictive coding to further reduce signal redundancy. We compare Multilayer Perceptron (MLP) and Convolutional Neural Network (CNN) predictors against a non-predictive baseline and a per-line Normalized Least Mean Squares (NLMS) linear predictor (similar to the MPEG-2 AAC Main Profile predictor).

items.title: M5-TTS: A Mini-Scale Multilingual and Multi-Dialect Text-to-Speech Language Model with Multi-Token Prediction
items.summary: We present M5-TTS, a compact text-to-speech system supporting multilingual and Chinese multidialect synthesis, zero-shot voice cloning, speaker-specific multilingual generation, and CPU streaming. Its 50M-parameter language model, excluding the speech codec, combines a temporal backbone with a local multi-token prediction module over 16 codebooks.

items.title: LSRP*: Scalable and Anytime Planning for Multi-Agent Path Finding with Asynchronous Actions
items.summary: Multi-Agent Path Finding (MAPF) seeks collision-free paths for multiple agents from their respective starting locations to their respective goal locations while minimizing path costs. To get rid of this assumption, recently, an algorithm called Loosely Synchronized Rule-based Planning (LSRP) was proposed, which can find sub-optimal solutions for many agents.

items.title: GUARD: Anomaly-Informed Q-Steering for Generative Robot Policies in Dexterous Manipulation
items.summary: Generative robot policies based on diffusion and flow matching can model complex, multimodal behaviors, but remain susceptible to covariate shift during closed-loop execution. We introduce GUARD, an anomaly-informed Q-steering framework that leverages the policy's training distribution to construct a dense, failure-anticipatory steering signal.

items.title: Mobility Information Capacity of Multi-Robot Systems: Safety-Aware Maneuver Design
items.summary: We develop a mobility information capacity (MIC) framework that jointly characterizes these two aspects. Mobility information is defined as the mutual information between a joint maneuver sequence and its noisy trajectory observation, and MIC maximizes this quantity under maneuver-resource constraints.

items.title: Who Taught the Robot That? Removing One User's Corrections from a Robot Policy That Learns Online
items.summary: A robot that keeps learning after deployment is corrected by several people in turn, and one of them may later ask to be removed. When users correct the robot by taking over control, an ordered log of training updates is enough: retraining on the remaining sessions in their original order gives a robot as close to the goal as training noise allows.

items.title: Look Only Where You Plan for Real-Time End-to-End Urban Driving
items.summary: Dense bird's-eye-view (BEV) construction accounts for 60% of the parameters in a strong recent driving planner. Evaluations on open-loop nuScenes, pseudo-simulated NAVSIM and closed-loop Bench2Drive show competitive planning with a compact representation.

items.title: OfficeTwin: Realizing 3D Reconstruction of Redundant Scenes through Partial Viewpoint Perception
items.summary: Feed-forward 3D reconstruction turns an uncalibrated monocular stream into a dense point cloud in a single inference pass, orders of magnitude faster than classical structure-from-motion (e.g., COLMAP), and reliable on the weakly textured, repetitive surfaces where keypoint matching fails outright.

items.title: DASH-SLAM: Calibration-Free Metric Monocular SLAM via Depth Scale Propagation
items.summary: Geometric foundation models estimate dense geometry and camera parameters from monocular images, but reliable SLAM also requires consistent scale and accurate data association across successive reconstructions. We present DASH-SLAM, a monocular SLAM system that integrates metric depth predictions from pretrained Depth Anything 3 into a shared-keyframe pose graph without task-specific fine-tuning.

items.title: Agibot: An Open-Source Modular Swerve-Drive Robot Platform for Agricultural Robotics Research and Education
items.summary: Agricultural production faces persistent labor shortages and increasing demand for automation, yet progress in agricultural robotics remains constrained by the limited availability of affordable, flexible, and accessible research platforms.

items.title: Capturability-Aware Footstep Planning in Cluttered Environments: A Recursively Feasible Sequential MPC on Axis-Aligned Safe Corridors
items.summary: A fundamental aspect of humanoid footstep planning is to jointly guarantee obstacle avoidance and locomotion stability. This paper presents a capturability-aware sequential Model Predictive Control (MPC) framework for Linear Inverted Pendulum (LIP)-based humanoid footstep planning in the presence of obstacles.

items.title: BATCH: Behavior Alignment for Cross-Embodiment Learning from Humans
items.summary: Human demonstrations provide a scalable source of diverse manipulation data, but leveraging them for robot learning remains challenging due to differences in embodiment, viewpoint, action spaces, and temporal structure. We introduce BATCH, a cross-embodiment learning framework that explicitly aligns human and robot behaviors.

items.title: A Unified Inertial Encoder for Human and Humanoid Motion
items.summary: Learning humanoid state estimation and language-grounded motion understanding from robot recordings ties training coverage to the robot's motion repertoire. To enable this transfer, we propose a unified inertial encoder whose shared inertial interface uses kinematic IMU synthesis to represent human and humanoid motion at corresponding body sites.

items.title: Beyond Semantic Classes: Online Physical Parameter Estimation via Embedding-Conditioned Gaussian Mixtures
items.summary: Enabling robots to infer interaction-relevant physical properties from vision before contact would improve planning and control in unstructured environments. Existing approaches often collapse this ambiguity to a point estimate or aggregate experience through fixed semantic classes, limiting their ability to preserve distinct physical regimes.

items.title: UniLatent: Cross-Embodiment Transfer via Latent Observation Alignment
items.summary: Robot datasets are costly to collect and are usually tied to a specific embodiment, making it difficult to reuse demonstrations across robots with different geometry, appearance, and kinematics. We introduce UniLatent, a cross-embodiment transfer framework that reduces the embodiment-induced observation gap in a shared latent space.

items.title: Efficient Learning of Differentiable MPC Policies on the GPU via Smoothed ADMM and First-Order Reinforcement Learning
items.summary: Differentiable model predictive control (MPC) enables structured, constraint-aware policies to be optimized end-to-end. We first introduce SmoothedTurboMPC, a GPU-parallel differentiable MPC solver combining sequential quadratic programming (SQP) with a log-barrier-smoothed alternating direction method of multipliers (ADMM) inner solver.

items.title: Preference-Augmented Distributional Reinforcement Learning for Risk-Sensitive Navigation
items.summary: Ensuring safe and reliable navigation under diverse sources of uncertainty remains a central challenge for autonomous systems. Within distributional reinforcement learning (DistRL), Implicit Quantile Networks (IQN) have attracted interest for navigation under uncertainty because they enable risk adaptation through flexible quantile sampling.

items.title: BiMuon: A Geometry-Aware Stochastic Bilevel Optimization Approach
items.summary: Stochastic bilevel optimization provides a general framework for many machine learning applications, such as hyperparameter learning, data reweighting, language model alignment, and actor-critic reinforcement learning.

items.title: Fast Accurate Quantum Monte Carlo without Metropolis Adjustment
items.summary: In quantum systems, physical quantities of interest can be expressed as expectation values of a probability distribution, which allows their estimation by Markov Chain Monte Carlo (MCMC) methods. This approach, an instance of Quantum Monte Carlo (QMC), plays a central role in obtaining predictions of system properties relevant to condensed matter and high energy physics.

items.title: Projected Neural Additive Models as Universal Approximators
items.summary: Neural additive models (NAMs) offer interpretability but lack expressivity due to their rigid additive structure, whereas multi-layer perceptrons (MLPs) achieve universal approximation at the cost of transparency.

items.title: Learning Across Heterogeneous Feature Spaces with Group Robustness
items.summary: In clinical applications, patients undergo different combinations of tests, and machine learning models must therefore ensure accurate predictions across heterogeneous feature spaces. Moreover, when patients' feature spaces are fully disjoint, current methods reduce to training independent models, preventing knowledge transfer across them.

items.title: TrialJev: Open-Weight Single Pass Eligibility Scoring for Patient Trial Screening
items.summary: Clinical trial screening requires assessing large numbers of patient-trial pairs to prioritize candidates for detailed eligibility review, often under restrictions on sharing patient records. We introduce TrialJev, an open-weight eligibility scorer that uses LoRA-adapted Qwen models and a pointer head to score natural-language answer options in a single forward pass, without autoregressive decoding.

items.title: Coordinated Mixed-Precision KV Cache Quantization for Efficient LLM-based Multi-agent Systems
items.summary: LLM-based multi-agent systems solve complex tasks through collaboration, but their growing, simultaneously resident key-value (KV) caches create a memory bottleneck. We introduce Coordinated Mixed-Precision KV Cache Quantization (CoMixKV), which combines online sensitivity estimation with joint agent-layer bit-width allocation under a shared memory budget.

items.title: Transferring local rib responses to new component geometries in sheet forming with a graph-based Transformer
items.summary: Sheet metal components often consist of a global geometry, such as the corner radii and forming depth of a corner component, and local features added to it. The local-feature effect is first learned on one global geometry, needing fewer simulations than learning all combinations, then transferred to other global geometries via transfer learning, which can need fewer target simulations than training from scratch.

items.title: fNIRSAtlas: A Large-Scale Benchmark for Functional Near-Infrared Spectroscopy Classification
items.summary: Functional near-infrared spectroscopy (fNIRS) is a promising modality for brain-computer interfaces and cognitive state decoding, but progress in machine learning for fNIRS has been limited by small, isolated datasets and inconsistent evaluation protocols. We evaluate a variety of baseline models from fNIRS and related neuroimaging and time-series machine learning literature on the benchmark.

items.title: All roads lead to Markov kernel networks: A representation theorem for discretization-stable learning
items.summary: Operator learning seeks to approximate function-to-function maps in a way that remains stable when the input discretization changes, a property sometimes called "discretization invariance".

items.title: Selected-Risk Calibration for Feasibility at Returned Decisions
items.summary: When an optimization problem uses a surrogate constraint, a decision that is feasible for the surrogate need not be feasible for the true constraint. We propose Selected-Risk Calibration (SRC), a framework that calibrates a learned constraint against the optimizer's returned decisions for objectives drawn from a given distribution.

items.title: Topological Deep Learning Challenge 2026: Bridging the Gap
items.summary: This paper describes the 2026 edition of the Topological Deep Learning Challenge: Bridging the Gap, hosted at the second Topology, Algebra, and Geometry in Data Science (TAG-DS) Conference.

items.title: Fresh Enough to Decide: Age of Intelligence for Cost-Aware Model Synchronization in Dynamic IoT Systems
items.summary: Resource-constrained IoT devices cache learned models for real-time decisions, but frequent updates incur substantial bandwidth, energy, and service overhead.

items.title: Causal Discovery Bench: Can LLMs Autonomously Conduct Effective Experiments?
items.summary: As large language model (LLM) agents get actively adopted for autonomous research, they must not only reason over existing evidence, but also design informative experiments, allocate resources, analyze sequential observations, and decide when to stop and make conclusions.

items.title: MAGE: Towards Generalizable Multi-timescale EEG Representations
items.summary: While current approaches, which largely build on EEG foundation models, have demonstrated strong performance across datasets and tasks, they typically rely on a fixed temporal scale. To address this limitation, we propose MAGE (\textbf{Multi-timescale Adaptive Generalization for EEG}), a foundation model that dynamically adapts to capture and integrate information across different timescales.

items.title: Process then Retrieve: Investigating the Origins of the Modality Gap in Vision-Language Models
items.summary: Understanding the origins of the modality gap in vision language models remains a significant challenge. We show that text tokens enter the model with much lower semantic density than visual tokens, driving early layers to focus on processing text representations before combining them with vision.

items.title: Ensemble Routing for Prompt-Adaptive Cost-Aware LLM Inference
items.summary: Large language models (LLMs) increasingly support Web-based services that must balance response quality and inference cost across heterogeneous requests. We introduce PISA, a prompt-adaptive, cost-aware single-model router, and PISA-E, its extension to ensemble routing.

items.title: Generative Active Learning for Label-Efficient Pan-Organ Ultrasound Diagnosis
items.summary: Medical ultrasound (US) enables real-time, non-invasive diagnosis, yet building US-based AI systems is limited by data scarcity, costly expert annotation, and limited cross-center generalizability.

items.title: AVCORP: Identifying and Resisting Deception via Communication Theory and Theory of Mind
items.summary: Today's LLM-based agents are vulnerable to deception by users and other agents. Defending against deception requires Theory of Mind (ToM) reasoning to infer the beliefs and goals of others as well as modeling tactics based on communication theory. To enable training models to detect deception, we adopt the well-known deception game, Avalon.

items.title: Key Institutional Considerations for Designing Effective Independent Verification Organizations
items.summary: Independent verification organizations (IVOs) have emerged as a popular, bipartisan solution for facilitating high-quality independent evaluations of AI technologies. But momentum is outpacing design: there is emerging consensus on the necessary operating conditions for robust IVOs, but little discourse on institutional and policy specifications to ensure those conditions are met.

items.title: AutoEMatic: Runtime-Adaptive Mixed-Precision LLM Inference via Automatic Exponent-Mantissa Refinement
items.summary: Existing LLM post-training quantization techniques determine precision before inference begins, yet the precision a model requires varies dynamically across prompts, layers, and inference phases. We realize AutoEMatic on two targets: GPU kernels that execute AutoFP on NVFP4 Tensor Cores, and an accelerator whose vector MAC datapath executes all AutoFP formats natively.

items.title: DeepResearch RewardBench: Evaluating Reward Models for Deep Research Report
items.summary: Empowered by Large Language Models (LLMs), deep research systems integrate online information into research reports through multi-step web searching and information synthesis. However, few studies have examined the effectiveness of existing reward models or LLMs in understanding and evaluating such research reports.

items.title: WorldMind: Test-Time Scaling for Visual Spatial Reasoning through Latent World Simulation
items.summary: Vision-Language Models (VLMs) have continuous deficiency in spatial reasoning tasks that require \emph{mental spatial transformation}, such as reasoning under hypothetical changes in viewpoint or position, known as perspective-taking tasks. We introduce \emph{WorldMind}, a framework for test-time scaling of spatial reasoning through latent world simulation.

items.title: What Is the Value of AI-Involved Art? Evidence From a Juried In-Person Exhibition
items.summary: What is the value of AI-involved art, and to whom does it belong? We begin to answer these questions using data from an in-person, juried AI art exhibition. We found that nearly half of evaluators reported willingness to buy an artwork, with pricing correlating with perceived artistic value---creativity and visual appeal---as well as the effort necessary to create it.

items.title: Homeopathic Learning: Diluting poisoned fine-tuning data can strengthen its effect
items.summary: We study homeopathic learning, a phenomenon where poisoned training data with little effect on its own can create a hidden backdoor once clean, contrasting data is added. Surprisingly, adding similarly formatted "clean" data not associated with T causes the model to learn T. This effect requires that the poison data have an identifying "trigger" feature that is absent from the clean data.

items.title: The Infrastructure Divide: Analyzing Community Stance on Data Center Development via Reddit
items.summary: The rapid expansion of AI-driven data center construction has outpaced public engagement: an estimated $64 billion in U.S. data center projects were blocked or delayed by local opposition between May 2024 and March 2025, yet the concerns driving this resistance remain poorly characterized.

items.title: META-IR: Meta-Introspective Reasoning for Adaptive Safety Alignment in LLM
items.summary: Large Language Models (LLMs) remain vulnerable to jailbreak attacks and harmful-content prompts, particularly under adversarial distribution shifts where static alignment pipelines fail to generalize. To overcome these limitations, this paper introduces META-IR, a meta-introspective reasoning framework that enhances safety alignment through meta-learning-driven adaptation.

items.title: AYO: A Safe and Privacy-Preserving Platform for Studying Children's Interaction with LLMs
items.summary: Children and adolescents are increasingly interacting with generative AI and large language models (LLMs), yet little is known about how these interactions may influence their development, beliefs, and behavior. Existing research has relied heavily on surveys, while direct study of children's interactions with LLMs presents substantial challenges related to safety, privacy, consent, and experimental control.

items.title: LoRazor: Trimming Adapter Execution for Efficient Multi-LoRA Serving
items.summary: LoRA offers a parameter-efficient adaptation strategy, supporting multi-user workloads via customized adapters on a shared backbone. Our motivational study reveals that employing LoRA adapters at every decoding step is unnecessary, releasing them early has limited impact on accuracy while substantially accelerating generation.

items.title: Veterans' Mental Health Crisis Severity Annotation: Do LLMs Agree More Than Human Experts?
items.summary: Large language models (LLMs) offer a scalable approach for annotating mental health and crisis-related social media content, but their reliability in safety-critical tasks remains unclear.

items.title: Don't Blame The Preferences: Examining The Emergence of Sycophancy in LLM Training
items.summary: AI sycophancy, the tendency of large language models (LLMs) to flatter users and affirm their beliefs, can undermine accuracy and contribute to misinformation, dependence, and overconfidence. We investigate sycophancy across the training pipelines of three model families and three benchmarks.
